blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the ovn_emit_need_to_frag option is enabled. It also depends on OVN support, and the OVN-side E/W fix is only in 24.09. Stable-series OVN versions may therefore not resolve the reported drops by default.

The original change introduced a regression (bug 2105383, wrong network_ids filter) that needed a follow-up revert. For stable branches the two commits were squashed. Any Ubuntu SRU must include both together, and the backport had conflicts and modified unit tests, so it needs careful verification.

No Ubuntu package or series information, test plan, or verification of the fix on the target Ubuntu release appears in the comments. The upstream stable backports exist only for 2024.2 and 2024.1, so older series may lack a backport.

blockers.summary: Reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been understood or reproduced from the boot side, so it is unclear the patch is the right fix. The original hanging-mount bug was reportedly resolved separately with mount namespaces.

The regression-potential section is wrong. It says os-prober is disabled by default, but it is automatically enabled when other OSes are detected at install time. The impact on those installs has to be reassessed.

The patch removes the fuseblk fallback without analysing what that path actually does. Filesystems that grub-probe cannot identify, but that fuseblk could mount and probe (for example NTFS or other FUSE-handled types), may stop being detected, so Windows or other OS entries could be lost.
The test plan only covers reproducing the LVM snapshot duplicate entry. It has no verification steps for the fixed package, and no regression test for dual-boot detection of other filesystems.

The description says the fix should later be backported to Noble and Jammy, but the SRU does not say which series it targets. It does not say how the mount-namespace change in Resolute relates to this fix, and it is unclear whether the patch applies to the older series.

There is no documented run of the test plan against the proposed package, and the PPA build version (3.0.0-0ubuntu1.5~ppa2) may differ from the final upload.
